What the numbers say

For the session of Thursday, November 5, 2026, the DappGo regime model reads the tracked universe (26 US-listed stocks and ETFs on DappGo's reviewed watchlist) as mixed. SPY is below its 50-day average and above its 200-day average; its 20-day trend is down and realised volatility is in the moderate band.

9 of 26 tickers (35%) are priced above their own 20-day moving average, and 12 of 25 (48%) above their 200-day average. That sits between the model's 30% and 55% breadth thresholds, so breadth alone decides nothing here. On the day 3 rose and 23 fell; the median move was −3.44%.

Among sectors with at least two tracked names, Communication had the strongest average move at −2.38% and Technology the weakest at −9.95%, a spread of 7.57 percentage points. The standard deviation of sector averages was 3.79 points; a larger figure means sectors moved less in step.

7 tickers have a 14-day RSI at or below 30 (EWT, INTC, MRVL, NVDA, TSM, GOOG and 1 more), and 1 at or above 70 (COST). An RSI extreme records how one-sided recent trading has been. It is not, by itself, evidence that the move is about to reverse.

Against the previous session in this archive (2026-11-04), the share of tickers above the 20-day average moved from 50% to 35%, and the regime reading changed from neutral to mixed.
